title.narrative: Multisectoral support in sites for internally displaced people in Adigrat, Eastern Zone, Tigray Region (Envelope 1)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed multisectoral project aims to address the urgent and interlinked humanitarian needs of internally displaced persons (IDPs) residing in both formal and informal settlements of Adigrat town, Eastern Tigray. Following years of conflict and repeated displacement, overcrowding, damaged infrastructure, and limited access to basic services have severely affected the living conditions and well-being of affected populations, particularly women, children, and persons with specific needs. Building on existing interventions, the project integrates five sectors: Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection (including GBV), and Emergency Shelter/NFIs, with Cash Assistance used as a flexible and dignified delivery modality wherever feasible.ltbrgtThe health component will strengthen primary healthcare delivery through the deployment and operation of Mobile Health Teams (MHTs), provision of essential medicines and medical equipment, and the establishment of effective referral pathways. The project will also support disease surveillance and outbreak response for cholera, measles, and other communicable diseases. Community health and hygiene promotion sessions will be conducted, with specific attention to maternal, newborn, and child health. Nutrition interventions include the screening of children and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) for malnutrition, provision of RUSF/CSB++ for MAM children, and distribution of supplementary rations and micronutrient supplements (vitamin A and iron-folate) to PLW. Capacity building for health professionals, Health Extension Workers (HEWs), and community volunteers will ensure quality and sustainability of services.ltbrgtTo improve access to safe water and sanitation in congested IDP settlements, the project will rehabilitate and maintain non-functional or damaged water systems, extend pipelines, and construct water distribution points and washing basins. Water quality testing, chlorination, and water treatment chemicals (including 70% HTH) will ensure safety at both source and household levels. Sanitation activities include the construction or rehabilitation of communal latrines and bathing facilities, desludging of latrines, and provision of incentives for attendants. Dedicated MHM and safety rooms for women and girls will be established. Hygiene promotion and cholera prevention campaigns will be conducted through community engagement and RCCE approaches, while WASHCOs will be strengthened and trained on operation and maintenance, ensuring community ownership and long-term functionality.ltbrgtProtection interventions will focus on enhancing safety, dignity, and psychosocial well-being of IDPs, especially women and girls at risk of GBV. Activities include vulnerability screening, GBV safety audits, community awareness campaigns, and capacity building of frontline service providers and local authorities. Women and Girls Friendly Spaces (WGFS) will be established and equipped to provide integrated services, including psychosocial support, case management, and referrals to One Stop Centres. Dignity kits will be distributed to women and girls of reproductive age, and multipurpose cash will be provided to GBV survivors and those at heightened risk.
